title: Denormalization Neglect of Tiny Cohesive Objects
pattern: Placing highly nested value objects or small tightly coupled attributes in separate tables, requiring SQL joins for every retrieval.
why_bad: It forces the database to perform costly table joins and separate disk seeks to load tiny value components that are always read and modified together.
detection: Multi-table relationships where the child tables represent immutable value objects containing only a few attributes.
counterexample: The value object is shared globally across millions of entities and is very large (e.g., product images). `Contextual`.
fix: Denormalize the value object attributes directly into the parent table's columns (or serialize as a LOB column).
source: *Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 5, Value Objects (p. 348) and *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 7 (p. 500).
